targets.name: CVRPLIB best-known-solution (BKS) updates: the X and XL capacitated vehicle routing sets plus the industrial Enpal instances
targets.what: A rolling, open leaderboard for the capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP). The site says 'Any person or group can submit improved solutions'; each one is checked and then added to the library. Open targets: (a) the 100 XL instances (1,000 to 10,000 customers), which exact methods cannot solve, so every improvement counts; (b) the 39 X instances (100 to 1,000 customers) that still lack proven optima; (c) industrial instances such as Enpal's Antwerp1, Flanders1 and Flanders2, last improved on 12 Sep 2026. The 30-day BKS Challenge on XL itself ran 12 Jan to 12 Feb 2026 and is over. Submissions to the library remain open.
targets.reward_or_value: No cash. Each accepted solution is published on CVRPLIB under the submitter's name, which is public third-party evidence of routing capability to show pilot customers. The BKS Challenge awarded certificates only.
targets.deadline: Rolling, with no deadline. The updates log shows activity on 11 and 12 Sep 2026.
targets.verifier: Deterministic. The CVRPLIB online checker validates feasibility and computes the objective, and the maintainers add verified solutions. Claims of new optimal solutions also need a citable method reference.
targets.eligibility: Anyone. The page says 'Any person or group can submit improved solutions.'
targets.ai_policy: No restriction on methods. The BKS Challenge page invites ML-based and hybrid methods and discusses AlphaEvolve explicitly. Precedent: on 11 Sep 2026 the 'Famou Agent Team, Baidu AI Cloud' was credited with 70 improved XL solutions (per the CVRPLIB updates page; the AI-agent reading comes from the team name, and the site does not describe the method). The same page notes that classic optimisation (FICO Xpress) beat four AlphaEvolve results weeks after publication, so strong classical baselines remain the bar.
targets.poc_cost: Compute only; estimate $100-500 of spot CPU. For scale, the initial XL BKSs came from published solvers running about 5 CPU-days per instance. Solver code (HGS-CVRP, FILO2, AILS-II) is open source. Claude Max covers the generation side.
targets.why_factory_fits: The best calibration arena for the industrial_opt evolver. It has a public deterministic evaluator, industrial-style instances (including a real company's), a live leaderboard, and a direct AI-agent competitor that has already won 70 BKSs (Baidu). Beating that is exactly the 'import OR literature plus evolve' loop the candidate sells to SMEs. The outcome is a realized, checkable result rather than an LLM-judge score, and routing is also the domain of the strongest vendor-reported AlphaEvolve customer claim: FM Logistic +10.4%.

targets.name: MIPLIB 2017 open instances (improved incumbents or solving an open instance)
targets.what: 212 mixed-integer programming instances that have not been reported solved, many from real industrial sources (e.g. Siemens 'sct1', 'tokyometro', dispatch and scheduling models). Two contributions count: a better incumbent (a better feasible solution) and closing an instance (a proof of optimality). The maintainers say contributions 'are always welcome' and publish them in periodic solufile updates. The latest update, on 24 Sep 2026, added 51 better incumbents; the one on 26 Jan 2026 added 40.
targets.reward_or_value: No cash. Contributors are credited in the official MIPLIB solution file, the reference benchmark used by solver vendors (Gurobi, FICO, Cplex, HiGHS, SCIP), which gives credibility with industrial buyers and solver-vendor partners.
targets.deadline: Rolling (periodic solufile releases).
targets.verifier: Deterministic. Solutions are checked with the MIPLIB solution checker and sent to miplibsolutions@zib.de. Moving an instance from open to solved needs a verifiable optimality proof.
targets.eligibility: Anyone.
targets.ai_policy: None stated. Only the verified solution counts.
targets.poc_cost: Estimate $100-1,000 of cloud CPU per campaign. Open-source solvers (SCIP, HiGHS) avoid licence cost; commercial solvers need their own licences.
targets.why_factory_fits: A second deterministic calibration track, for scheduling and MIP-style problems, that runs alongside routing. The factory can generate problem-specific primal heuristics, decompositions or reformulations for named industrial instances and have them verified by the checker. Each accepted incumbent is a realized result that can be cited in pilot sales. Because the ledger records instance-level outcomes, success rates from this track are not confounded by judge scoring.

targets.name: TrafficFlowBench, 2026 IEEE Big Data Cup (Kaggle community competition)
targets.what: A multi-task freeway-traffic benchmark: 10 directional corridors, 5-minute resolution, 11 months of synthetic records. Four tasks are scored with weights of 0.35 for state reconstruction of masked cells, 0.30 for 30-minute queue forecasting from 60 minutes of history, 0.15 for physics consistency (fundamental diagram and vehicle conservation) and 0.20 for origin-destination/path-flow estimation. This covers the forecasting and demand-estimation half of the industrial_opt domain.
targets.reward_or_value: USD 3,500 pool: Gold $1,500, Silver $1,000, Bronze $500, and a Student/Newcomer award of $500 (undergraduate or high-school teams only). Winners are also offered a slot to present and publish at IEEE BigData 2026 (Phoenix, 14-17 Dec 2026).
targets.deadline: Final submission 6 Nov 2026. Register by emailing trafficflowbench@gmail.com by 25 Oct 2026. Data was rebuilt on 11 Sep 2026; only submissions made after the rebuild are eligible for awards.
targets.verifier: The Kaggle private leaderboard with a fixed composite metric. Before any award, the organisers rerun the code end to end and check that it reproduces the submitted file. Near-identical entries across teams are disqualified.
targets.eligibility: Kaggle foundational rules: age 18+ (or age of majority), worldwide except sanctioned regions, teams of up to 4, one account per person.
targets.ai_policy: Allowed with disclosure. External data, pretrained models, AutoML tools and APIs are permitted if 'reasonably available to other participants at no or minimal cost'. Finalists must disclose every pretrained model and every paid or rate-limited API. A Claude-API step inside the prediction pipeline could fail the 'minimal cost' test. Using Claude to write the code is not restricted.
targets.poc_cost: Under $200 (estimate). The data is public, the tasks are tabular, and the work runs in Kaggle notebooks or on a laptop.
targets.why_factory_fits: A cheap, 5-week, externally scored test of the forecasting and physics-constrained estimation side of the pilot offering. It uses a hidden holdout and a reproducibility check, the same verification shape as a customer's held-out KPI. The cash is small, so treat it as calibration with a publication upside rather than revenue.

targets.name: Innovate UK: Frontier AI: SME Champions, Phase 1
targets.what: Grant for UK SME feasibility studies of 'frontier AI' innovations with state-of-the-art benchmarked results. Relevant priorities include Theme 1, 'medicines manufacturing optimisation', and Theme 2, 'multi objective optimisation' and 'data efficient learning for materials process optimisation and manufacturing scale up'. Deliverables: a proof-of-concept, validation against a named baseline with numeric targets, and a technical whitepaper. Phase 1 feeds a Phase 2 of up to £1M (subject to UKRI business-case approval).
targets.reward_or_value: Share of £3.1M. Total project cost must be £150,000-£250,000, with grant up to 70% for micro and small firms (60% for medium). Innovate UK estimates about a 2% chance of success.
targets.deadline: Opens 1 Oct 2026, closes 11 Nov 2026 at 11:00 UK time. Briefing on 7 Oct 2026.
targets.verifier: Innovate UK expert assessment of the application. The project's own validation must use pre-defined metrics against named baselines, which suits executed OR benchmarks.
targets.eligibility: Must lead alone as a UK-registered micro, small or medium enterprise. One application per SME. No subcontractors. The project must last 1-3 months, start by 1 Apr 2027 and end by 30 Jun 2027. Work must be done and exploited in the UK. Starting TRL must be 1-3.
targets.ai_policy: The UKRI generative-AI policy (updated 6 Jul 2026) lets applicants use generative AI but expects transparency about non-minimal use, and assessors may not use it. In scope, the competition excludes 'routine integration... of existing AI tools or third party models without novel AI or ML development'. A Claude-wrapper pitch would be out of scope: the novelty must be in the core algorithm (e.g. the evolver or search mechanism) with defensible IP.
targets.poc_cost: Preparing the application costs team time plus under $500 of benchmark compute (estimate). If awarded, the SME funds 30% of the £150-250k project.
targets.why_factory_fits: Non-dilutive money that would fund the first industrial-optimisation pilots, with a named, benchmarked baseline for medicines- or materials-manufacturing process optimisation. It needs a concrete industrial use case with measured baselines, which CVRPLIB/MIPLIB calibration results and a partner KPI could supply. The 2% base rate makes this a lottery ticket, not a plan.

targets.name: NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I (solicitation NSF 26-510)
targets.what: US federal seed grant for high-risk technical R&D in 'nearly all technology areas' (AI-driven industrial optimisation is eligible). The programme was reauthorised through 30 Sep 2031 and restarted in 2026. A Phase I proposal needs an official invitation first, obtained by submitting a Project Pitch.
targets.reward_or_value: Phase I up to $305,000 for 6-18 months. The route leads to Phase II (up to $1.25M, per secondary reporting of the solicitation).
targets.deadline: Full-proposal windows on 4 Nov 2026, 4 Mar 2027 and 7 Jul 2027. Invitations are valid for the next two deadlines, so a pitch sent now realistically targets 4 Mar 2027.
targets.verifier: NSF merit review, after the Project Pitch invitation.
targets.eligibility: Small business concern with at most 500 employees including affiliates. The PI must be primarily (51%+) employed by the company and have a legal right to work in the US. Under SBA rules (13 CFR 121.702, not restated on the NSF page), the company must be over 50% owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents. A UK-only company is ineligible without a US entity that meets this.
targets.ai_policy: NSF's notice on generative AI in merit review encourages proposers to state in the project description whether and how generative AI was used. Reviewers may not upload proposal content to non-approved AI tools.
targets.poc_cost: Pitch and proposal cost team time only (under $500, estimate). If US ownership is lacking, restructuring costs are outside the POC budget.
targets.why_factory_fits: This is the follow-on route already listed in the candidate's value path. It suits a demonstrated evolver-plus-evaluator service with pilot evidence. It only applies if OptiLex has, or creates, a qualifying US-owned entity; otherwise treat it as not actionable.

targets.name: Topcoder Marathon Match Tournament 2026: Marathon Match 168
targets.what: A one-week heuristic-optimisation match. These are usually NP-hard problems with no known optimum, scored automatically on hidden test cases. MM 168 is part of a tournament (1 Jun 2026 to 31 Mar 2027, at least 6 matches); points accumulate, and the top 12 go to a 24-hour online final.
targets.reward_or_value: Cash goes only to tournament finalists: champion $6,000, 2nd $2,000, 3rd $500, 4th-8th $200 each. Single matches carry leaderboard points, not money. A late entrant can play only about 4 remaining matches, so reaching the final is unlikely.
targets.deadline: MM 168: 25 Nov to 2 Dec 2026 (2:00 AM EST). MM 167 (7-14 Oct) falls before the 15 Oct cut-off. The tournament counts matches until 31 Mar 2027.
targets.verifier: Automatic system tests on a large hidden test set, using the match's published scoring function.
targets.eligibility: Topcoder members who meet Topcoder's Terms and Conditions to receive prizes.
targets.ai_policy: The official tournament rules page does not mention AI. Topcoder help describes matches as open-ended optimisation without method rules. Check the MM 168 problem statement for any AI clause before relying on automated agent loops. (By contrast, AtCoder Heuristic Contests restrict agents from iterating on execution results, and short AHCs now largely prohibit generative AI, so AtCoder is excluded.)
targets.poc_cost: Under $100 (estimate). Scoring runs on Topcoder infrastructure, and local testing takes laptop-scale compute.
targets.why_factory_fits: A fast, hidden-test, deterministic benchmark for the evolver on a new problem each time. It tests transfer to unseen problems, which matters for a domain-agnostic engine. The prize money is small and hard to reach this late, so value it as calibration only.

(2) Email registration does not gate data access; it records participation for the workshop. (3) The Student/Newcomer award needs every team member to be an enrolled high-school or undergraduate student on 6 Nov 2026. (4) The public leaderboard scores only the validation month; final standings come from a different month. Status: 201 teams and 2,374 submissions so far.

checks.name: Innovate UK: Frontier AI: SME Champions, Phase 1
checks.correction: All details verified on the official page. It opens 1 Oct 2026 (not yet open as of 27 Sep) and closes 11 Nov 2026 at 11:00. The pot is £3.1M, projects cost £150k-£250k, and grant is up to 70% for micro/small firms and 60% for medium. Applicants must be a UK SME applying alone, with no subcontractors and only one application per SME. Projects last 1-3 months, start by 1 Apr 2027, end by 30 Jun 2027, start at TRL 1-3, and must be done and exploited in the UK. The page states a 2% chance of success. The briefing is on 7 Oct, and applicants are notified on 26 Jan 2027. Phase 2 funds 12-month demonstrators up to £1M. Exclusions include 'routine integration, deployment, orchestration or productization of existing AI tools or third party models without novel AI or ML development' and proposals without a named baseline with numeric targets. The UKRI generative-AI policy date (6 Jul 2026) was not separately verified.

checks.name: NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I (solicitation NSF 26-510)
checks.correction: Verified: Phase I is up to $305,000 for 6-18 months. Phase II is up to $1,250,000, typically for 24 months; this is stated in the solicitation itself, not only in secondary reporting. Fast-Track is up to $1,555,000, and the page says each company can receive up to $2M for R&D. Deadlines are 4 Nov 2026, 4 Mar 2027 and 7 Jul 2027. A Project Pitch invitation is required and is valid for the next two deadlines. The limit is 500 employees, and the PI must be 51% or more employed by the company with a legal right to work in the US. The relaunch follows the Small Business Innovation and Economic Security Act, which also creates Strategic Breakthrough awards for Phase II awardees. Not on the page: the 30 Sep 2031 reauthorisation date, the US-ownership rule (SBA 13 CFR 121.702, correctly flagged as external), and the generative-AI disclosure notice. The page mentions foreign-risk due diligence. Ineligible for a UK-only OptiLex entity without a qualifying US-owned small business.

checks.name: Topcoder Marathon Match Tournament 2026: Marathon Match 168
checks.correction: Verified on the official schedule: MM 167 runs 7-14 Oct 2026 and MM 168 runs 25 Nov-2 Dec 2026, both at 2:00 AM EST; MM 165 and 166 are complete. The rules page has the tournament window of 1 Jun 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 (a match must open and close inside it to count), the top 12 by points advancing, and a 24-hour online final with 30 minutes of setup. The prize table (rendered from the page's SVG image) is Champion $6,000, 2nd $2,000, 3rd $500 and 4th-8th $200, which matches the target. The rules do not mention AI. Caveats: '15 Oct cut-off' does not appear on any Topcoder page, so it must be an internal planning date. 'At least 6 matches' appears only in a worked scoring example, not as a stated minimum.

targets.name: NIH PAR-25-374: Translational Bioinformatics and Experimental Approaches to Advance Drug Repositioning and Combination Therapy Development for AD/ADRD (R01, clinical trial not allowed)
targets.what: An NIA funding opportunity for rigorous preclinical proof-of-concept testing, in mouse or cell-based AD/ADRD models, of approved or investigational drugs and drug combinations that data-driven approaches predict will work in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. Combinations with non-drug interventions also qualify. The notice says computational and AI/ML methods have already found hundreds of repurposable candidates; what is missing is prioritising them and testing them rigorously in vivo or in vitro.
targets.reward_or_value: An R01 grant with direct costs capped at $1M per year (grants.gov lists an award ceiling of $1,000,000). Budgets must match actual project needs. Co-authored papers and follow-on NIA funding, for example through the ACTDRx AD program pipeline.
targets.deadline: Next new-application due date is 8 Feb 2027 (the 6 Oct 2026 date has passed). Later dates are 9 Jun 2027, 8 Oct 2027 and 7 Feb 2028. The NOFO expires in May 2028 (grants.gov close date 7 May 2028).
targets.verifier: NIH peer review first, then the funded work itself: PK/PD and efficacy of the predicted drugs or combinations against AD/ADRD outcomes in mouse or cell models, measured molecularly, biochemically, neuropathologically and functionally. Before submission, a partner lab's cell assay gives the preliminary data.
targets.eligibility: Broad. Universities, nonprofits, small businesses and for-profits are eligible, and foreign (non-US) organisations ARE eligible under this NOFO, which matters for a UK-based team. Applicants need a PI at an organisation registered in SAM, eRA Commons and grants.gov, with an NCAGE code for foreign organisations; registration can take 6 weeks or more.
targets.ai_policy: NIH NOT-OD-25-132 says NIH will not treat applications 'substantially developed by AI, or contain sections substantially developed by AI' as the applicants' original ideas. If AI use is detected after award, it can be referred to the Office of Research Integrity. There is also a cap of 6 applications per PI per calendar year. The NOFO itself welcomes AI/ML-identified candidates, so the hypothesis can come from AI, but a human PI must write the application.
targets.poc_cost: Factory side is about $0-2k (Max plus API) to generate, deduplicate and rank candidates against the literature, ClinicalTrials.gov and the ACTDRx AD resources. A partner lab pays for preliminary cell-assay data, typically a few thousand dollars in reagents. The grant then funds the mouse work.
targets.why_factory_fits: This is the closest thing to a posted 'buyer' for exactly what the factory makes: data-driven repositioning and combination hypotheses that need prioritising and then testing. Foreign eligibility and a rolling three-times-a-year cycle through 2028 fit a UK team with an academic partner. Co-Scientist's lab-validated repurposing results (AML in vitro, liver-fibrosis organoids) are the precedent. The main risk is NIH's AI-originality rule, so the partner PI must own the idea and write the application.

targets.name: NIH/NCATS RFA-TR-25-002: Preclinical Proof of Concept Studies for Rare Diseases (R21, clinical trial not allowed)
targets.what: NCATS funds efficacy studies with PK/PD in an established, validated rare-disease model to show that a proposed therapeutic, explicitly including repurposed or repositioned drugs, warrants further development. The goal is to reach the point where the project attracts IND-enabling investment or, for repurposing, moves into clinical trials. Model development is not funded. Applicants must show they have access to the model (with a letter or a quote) and a plan for a rare-disease steering committee.
targets.reward_or_value: Up to $275,000 in direct costs over 2 years (no more than $200,000 in any one year). Rare-disease repurposing then leads to foundation, CWR or venture follow-on funding.
targets.deadline: 2 Jun 2027 (extended by NOT-TR-26-009). The NOFO expires 3 Jun 2027. Review is in Oct 2027, council in Jan 2028, and the earliest start in Apr 2028.
targets.verifier: NIH peer review, then in-vivo or advanced in-vitro efficacy with PK/PD in a validated rare-disease model. Tissue-chip and microphysiological models are allowed.
targets.eligibility: US organisations, including small businesses and for-profits. Foreign organisations are NOT eligible, and foreign subawards are not allowed, though foreign components and consultants are. The factory would need a US academic or small-business partner that already has the disease model.
targets.ai_policy: The same NIH rules apply (NOT-OD-25-132). Applications substantially developed by AI are not treated as original, and each PI may submit at most 6 applications per calendar year. The RFA has no specific AI rule.
targets.poc_cost: About $0-2k for the factory to produce rare-disease repurposing dossiers: mechanism rationale, a deduplication and patent check, and a list of labs that hold validated models. The partner lab provides the model and any pilot data.
targets.why_factory_fits: Rare diseases are where AI repurposing faces the least competition (under 5% of rare diseases have treatments, per the NOFO). The model-access requirement also tells the factory whom to target: labs that already have validated models but lack a candidate drug. The long lead time to Jun 2027 leaves room to recruit a partner. It is weaker than PAR-25-374 because only US organisations can apply.

targets.name: UKRI Translation: MRC Proof of Concept, stage one (successor to the Developmental Pathway Funding Scheme)
targets.what: MRC translational funding for developing and testing new interventions, from prototype through phase 2a. 'Medicines repurposing studies' are explicitly in scope: clinical studies, or pre-clinical activities where regulators require them. Stage one is an outline; successful applicants are invited to a full stage-two application.
targets.reward_or_value: No funding limit; costs must suit the project. UKRI pays 80% of full economic cost (100% for permitted exceptions). International high-income-country costs are capped at 30%.
targets.deadline: Stage one closes 18 Nov 2026 at 4pm UK time; the stage-one panel meets 21 Jan 2027. Stage two runs 5 Nov 2026 to 3 Mar 2027, or can be deferred to the round opening 4 Mar 2027 (closing 7 Jul 2027). The scheme has multiple deadlines each year (March, July, November).
targets.verifier: MRC expert panel review, which requires 'sufficient proof of concept data'. The funded pre-clinical or clinical repurposing study is then the realized validation.
targets.eligibility: Only researchers employed by an eligible UK research organisation can be Project Lead. Businesses and charities cannot lead unless they are approved UKRI Independent Research Organisations. International co-leads may take part.
targets.ai_policy: UKRI: 'Use of generative AI tools to prepare funding applications is permitted, however, caution should be applied.' Reviewers may not use generative AI.
targets.poc_cost: About $0-2k for the factory. Proof-of-concept data must already exist, for example the partner lab's cell or organoid assay on a factory-proposed drug, at the lab's cost. Clinical repurposing work would be funded by the award.
targets.why_factory_fits: This is the most AI-tolerant of the major public funders (generative AI allowed with caution, unlike NIH and CWR). It is UK-based and fits the team's location. It explicitly funds repurposing through to phase 2a, and it is a good follow-on once a partner lab has confirmed an in-vitro hit. The 18 Nov 2026 deadline only works if a partner already has data. Otherwise, target the Mar or Jul 2027 rounds.

targets.name: Michael J. Fox Foundation: Parkinson's Disease Therapeutics Pipeline Program (rolling pre-proposals)
targets.what: MJFF funds preclinical and clinical therapeutic development for Parkinson's disease. The RFA says applicants 'may also propose testing of repurposed or repositioned therapies' with robust biomarker-enabled testing. A pre-proposal can be submitted at any time, and MJFF reviews it within 3 weeks. Selected applicants are invited to a full proposal and hear a decision within about 3 months.
targets.reward_or_value: $250,000 to more than $2M in the current RFA overview; the program page says up to $5M. The budget covers direct and indirect costs, with indirect costs capped at 15% for academic and 10% for for-profit institutions. Projects run 1-2 years (preclinical) or 2-3 years (clinical).
targets.deadline: Rolling pre-proposals. The funding-opportunities page lists the program as rolling as of 2026-09-27. The last published full-proposal dates ended 25 Jun 2026; invited applicants get new cycles.
targets.verifier: MJFF staff review within 3 weeks is a fast and cheap first filter. After that come the funded efficacy and biomarker studies in relevant in-vitro or in-vivo models, then clinical proof of concept.
targets.eligibility: Industry groups, or academic teams working with a dedicated industry partner able to develop the drug commercially (academic-led exemptions in some cases). Worldwide. Training and fellowships are not supported.
targets.ai_policy: No AI policy found on the program page or in the RFA. MJFF's Open Science Policy requires funded outputs to be openly shared with persistent identifiers.
targets.poc_cost: About $0-500 for the factory to write a pre-proposal dossier once a partner exists. Preliminary validation data from an academic or biotech partner would strengthen it.
targets.why_factory_fits: This is the fastest official feedback loop found: a 3-week expert verdict on a rolling basis, with resubmission after feedback encouraged. That makes it usable as an outcome-ledger signal for repurposing ideas. The catch is that it needs an industry or academic-plus-industry team, so the factory would pitch pairs of candidate and partner (for example a small biotech that holds a repurposable asset) rather than bare hypotheses.

targets.name: Arc Institute Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 (zero-shot perturbation-response prediction)
targets.what: Entrants predict CRISPRi knockdown transcriptional responses (Perturb-seq) in 6 previously unseen cell lines, using only each line's unperturbed state. It is zero-shot, with no task training set. Three lines drive the live validation leaderboard and three are held out for the final test. Entrants may use any modelling strategy and any public or proprietary data.
targets.reward_or_value: $175,000 in prizes: $100,000 first, $50,000 second, $25,000 third, paid as a mix of cash and NVIDIA Brev credits. Sponsors are NVIDIA, 10x Genomics and Ultima Genomics. Winning also brings visibility in the virtual-cell and target-discovery community.
targets.deadline: Final test set released 22 Oct 2026; submissions due 5 Nov 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Winners announced mid-to-late November 2026.
targets.verifier: Fully computational: aggregate score across 6 metrics on held-out, lab-generated Perturb-seq data from Arc. No partner lab is needed.
targets.eligibility: Individuals, academic labs, companies and independent research organisations.
targets.ai_policy: Open: 'any modeling strategy', trained on any data. No restriction on AI-generated or AI-assisted work was found.
targets.poc_cost: Under $2k: Claude Max for a pipeline built with agents plus modest GPU time (Brev or Modal) for embedding or regression models on public Perturb-seq data. The time budget is 5 weeks.
targets.why_factory_fits: The fit with drug repurposing is partial. The perturbations are genetic knockdowns, not drugs, so the challenge tests the mechanism and target reasoning behind repurposing hypotheses, not repurposing itself. It is, however, the only target in this domain with a cheap, objective, lab-grounded verifier and no partner lab. That makes it a way to calibrate the bio generator and critics before spending partner goodwill. Opus 5.5's biology-classifier fallback may weaken outputs on some prompts.

targets.name: Anthropic AI for Science Program (API credits, rolling monthly review)
targets.what: Free Claude API credits for high-impact research, especially in biology and life sciences, including hypothesis generation and experiment design. Applications are made through a Google Form and pass a biosecurity screen.
targets.reward_or_value: Up to $20,000 in API credits over 6 months per approved application (help-center page). This is compute, not cash. The larger tracks announced in 2026 are closed: the Claude Science track (up to $30k, closed 15 Jul 2026) and rare-disease grants (up to $50k, closed 2 Aug 2026).
targets.deadline: Rolling. Submissions are evaluated on the first Monday of each month.
targets.verifier: Anthropic's review of scientific merit, impact, feasibility, team credentials and biosecurity. It enables work but does not validate ideas. The real verifier is still the partner lab's assays.
targets.eligibility: The help center says researchers at academic and nonprofit institutions. The official rules require age 18+ with institutional consent and exclude residents of sanctioned countries. In practice the factory needs an academic or nonprofit PI partner to apply.
targets.ai_policy: AI use is the point of the program. Grantees are not exempt from Anthropic's Usage Policy ('do not receive exemption from our Usage Policy'), so Opus 5.5 biology-classifier fallback still applies. Only the closed rare-disease track mentioned possible classifier exemptions.
targets.poc_cost: $0. It offsets API spend beyond the Max subscription for large-scale literature, patent and trial-registry deduplication and generation runs.
targets.why_factory_fits: This is not a value channel in itself, but it is the cheapest way to fund API-heavy generation and deduplication once a partner PI is recruited, which keeps the factory under the roughly $2k-per-POC budget. It is also a natural first step in recruiting a partner lab: a joint credit application costs the PI little and tests commitment before any assay money is spent.

checks.name: NIH PAR-25-374: Translational Bioinformatics and Experimental Approaches to Advance Drug Repositioning and Combination Therapy Development for AD/ADRD (R01, clinical trial not allowed)

The following were confirmed through the grants.gov API (opp 357943): status posted, open date 30 Dec 2024, close date 7 May 2028, NIH expiration 8 May 2028, award ceiling $1,000,000, and 'Non-domestic (non-U.S.) Entities (Foreign Organizations)' listed as eligible with no exclusion text. checks.name: NIH/NCATS RFA-TR-25-002: Preclinical Proof of Concept Studies for Rare Diseases (R21, clinical trial not allowed)
checks.correction: Minor note, no substantive error. NOT-TR-26-009 (issued 5 Jun 2026) extended the RFA by one council round: due date 2 Jun 2027, expiration 3 Jun 2027. The budget of $275k direct over 2 years with at most $200k in any year, and the repurposing scope, were confirmed via a secondary summary. The NIH page is behind a Cloudflare challenge, so it was verified through grants.gov and search snippets.

checks.name: UKRI Translation: MRC Proof of Concept, stage one (successor to the Developmental Pathway Funding Scheme)
checks.correction: Confirmed on the UKRI page: status Open, opened 2 Jul 2026, closes 18 Nov 2026 at 4pm UK time, stage-one panel 21 Jan 2027. There is no funding limit, and UKRI pays 80% of FEC (100% for exceptions). International costs for high-income countries are capped at 30% (DAC-list countries are uncapped). Medicines repurposing is explicitly in scope. Generative AI is permitted with caution, and reviewers may not use it. Stage two is due 3 Mar 2027, or can be deferred to 7 Jul 2027. checks.name: Michael J. Fox Foundation: Parkinson's Disease Therapeutics Pipeline Program (rolling pre-proposals)
checks.correction: (1) Deadlines: full-proposal cycles did NOT end on 25 Jun 2026. The 2026 overview PDF lists 20 Aug 2026, 30 Oct 2026 and 8 Jan 2027. (2) Reward: the 2026 overview PDF gives $1M-$5M, tiered by stage. The program page says $250k to more than $5M. The '$250k to more than $2M' figure is wrong. Otherwise an industry partner or an academic-industry team is required. checks.name: Arc Institute Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 (zero-shot perturbation-response prediction)
checks.correction: Confirmed on the Arc news page: zero-shot prediction of CRISPRi knockdown responses in 6 unseen cell lines (3 for validation, 3 for the final test), no training set. Prizes are $100k, $50k and $25k, paid as a mix of cash and NVIDIA Brev credits, with sponsors NVIDIA, 10x Genomics and Ultima Genomics. The validation leaderboard launched 20 Aug.
